name: wincode (bincode-compatible serializer)
verdict_reason: Writing bincode 1.3.3's format (identical output sizes on log and mesh), wincode 0.6.0 serialized 3.3x-32.7x faster and deserialized 1.12x-25.9x faster in the independent 2026-08-07 run, with the large gains on float-heavy mesh data. bincode stopped development in 2025-12 and its maintainers list wincode as an alternative.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmark with public code; rustc nightly, the CPU and lto = true are stated.
claimed_speedup: Serialize 140.61 µs vs 464.75 µs (log), 148.62 µs vs 4.8569 ms (mesh), 140.23 µs vs 518.86 µs (minecraft_savedata); deserialize 1.4340 ms vs 1.6158 ms, 140.71 µs vs 3.6395 ms, 1.3652 ms vs 1.5229 ms; 3.3x-32.7x serialize, 1.12x-25.9x deserialize (ratios derived from page data)
workload: rust_serialization_benchmark log, mesh and minecraft_savedata datasets; serialize into a pre-sized buffer and deserialize into owned types; wincode derives SchemaWrite/SchemaRead, bincode 1.3.3 uses serde.
toolchain: rustc 1.99.0-nightly (2026-08-06), bench profile lto = true, no target-cpu flag
one_liner: Drop-in for bincode 1's wire format that serializes 3x-33x and deserializes 1.1x-26x faster than bincode 1.3.3 through serde.
how_it_is_fast: Derive macros generate SchemaWrite/SchemaRead code that writes fields straight into the output buffer and initializes values in place when reading, instead of going through serde's Serializer and Visitor layers. The README describes the design as focused on in-place initialization and direct memory writes.
use_it_when: Replacing bincode 1.x where existing stored or on-the-wire bytes must stay readable
Plain-data-heavy payloads such as float arrays, where the gap was 26x-33x
skip_it_when: String-heavy data where deserialization only gained 1.12x-1.13x; consider bitcode if you can change the format
Types that only implement serde traits and cannot take wincode's derives
caveats: Compatibility is per configuration: on minecraft_savedata the benchmark recorded 566975 bytes for wincode vs 569975 for bincode 1.3.3, so check your types
Single run on a shared runner; bincode was removed from later runs
speedy, rkyv and wincode all land near 140-150 µs on mesh while bincode 1.3.3 takes about 4.9 ms, so much of the mesh gap reflects bincode-through-serde's per-element cost on float arrays
tradeoffs: Newer crate (0.x) maintained by Anza; v0.1.2 had three external security reviews per the README

evidence.quote: Fast, bincode‑compatible serializer/deserializer focused on in‑place initialization and direct memory writes.
Due to a doxxing and harassment incident, the bincode team has taken the decision to cease development permanently.
